claims.text: Nanoscale chromium short-range ordering at grain boundaries and interfaces promotes rapid formation of a protective Cr2O3 layer in stainless and low-alloy steels.
Molybdenum short-range ordering contributes, to a lesser extent than chromium ordering, to protective oxide formation.
The Cr-rich oxide formed as a result of short-range ordering is stable and self-healing.
The proposed Cr-rich oxide suppresses both uniform and localized corrosion.
Conventional Cr-containing austenitic and low-alloy steels have relatively homogeneous, chemically disordered solid solutions before treatment.
Controlled annealing can enhance chromium short-range ordering and induce nanoscale compositional clustering.
Chromium can segregate or develop nanoscale chemical heterogeneity at crystalline defects in austenitic stainless steel.
Annealing-induced Cr-enriched clusters occur specifically at grain boundaries and near-surface regions.
Cr-enriched clusters at grain boundaries and near-surface regions serve as preferential oxidation sites.
Enhanced chromium short-range ordering lowers the energy barrier for Cr2O3 formation.
Enhanced chromium short-range ordering produces a denser and more adherent passive film.
Atomic ordering minimizes defects in the oxide scale.
Fewer defects in the oxide scale reduce electrolyte penetration and anodic dissolution.
Chromium short-range ordering promotes passive-film self-healing after mechanical or chemical damage.
Steels treated to enhance chromium short-range order will have lower corrosion-current density than untreated steels under identical aggressive conditions.
Steels treated to enhance chromium short-range order will have reduced corrosion-related weight loss and more stable passivation than untreated steels.
Chemically disordered untreated steels form less protective and less uniform passive oxide layers.
The proposed effect applies in aggressive aqueous chemical-processing environments and oxidizing high-temperature, high-pressure reactor water.
The influence of chromium short-range ordering may diminish when irradiation-induced transmutation or high-temperature carburization predominates.
Grain size, inclusion content, and additional alloying elements also influence steel corrosion resistance and may confound the isolated effect of chromium short-range ordering.
